statement: Build a single-file HTML, CSS and JavaScript portfolio site for a wedding photographer. Its main job is to turn visitors into inquiries, with the gallery supporting that. The look is light, editorial and minimal. All photos, copy and contact details are clearly labeled, swappable placeholders, so the site is structure complete but not publishable until real content replaces them.
audience: Engaged couples looking for a wedding photographer
standards: One file of plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no build step; CDN libraries are allowed
Light, editorial, minimal design where the photos carry the page
Every placeholder is visibly labeled and easy to find and swap
No invented facts: no made-up names, prices, testimonials, awards or credentials
rules: Inquiry is the primary call to action; the gallery supports it
Do not publish prices or packages
The form endpoint or mailto address is a marked placeholder; no real third-party account or address is invented
Open inputs appear on the site as marked placeholders and never block done
done_when: The site is one HTML file with its CSS and JavaScript inline and no build step; any external resource is a CDN link
The page has a gallery section with at least six image slots, each visibly labeled as a placeholder
The page has an about section whose copy is visibly marked as sample copy
The page has a prominent inquiry section with a form containing name, email and message fields and a submit button, and its endpoint or mailto target is marked as a placeholder
A visible inquiry call to action near the top of the page links to the inquiry section
Contact details (email) are visible on the page and marked as placeholders
The CSS sets a light page background and a minimal, photo-led layout, with no dark or full-bleed cinematic theme
The file contains no prices, packages or invented testimonials
Every open input is visibly marked as a placeholder where it appears in the file
open_inputs: Real wedding photos for the gallery
Form submission endpoint (third-party service) or the mailto address to use
